name: PWM & Dead-time Calculator
blurb: timer PSC/ARR for a PWM frequency and resolution, and the dead-time register for a half bridge
intro: Picks PSC and ARR for a PWM frequency with the most duty resolution, gives CCR for the duty, and encodes the dead time into TIMx_BDTR.DTG with its real value, per the STM32 reference manuals' formulas; optionally suggests the dead time from MOSFET and driver delays (Infineon AN2007-04).

inputs.label: Timer clock
inputs.help: TIM1/TIM8 kernel clock: APB2 timer clock (x2 when the APB2 prescaler is not 1). F407: 168 MHz, F103: 72 MHz, G474: 170 MHz.

inputs.label: Clock division CKD
options: Auto (smallest that reaches the dead time)

inputs.label: Prescaler (PSC)
inputs.help: Empty = the smallest PSC, for the most resolution.

inputs.label: Suggest dead time from switch timings

examples.title: STM32F407 TIM1, 20 kHz center-aligned motor PWM, 500 ns dead time
STM32F103 TIM1, 16 kHz edge-aligned, dead time from IR2110 + MOSFET timings

usage: Give fclk (timer clock, Hz), freq (Hz), mode (center|edge), duty (%), deadtime (ns), ckd (auto|1|2|4), complementary, width (16|32), optionally psc to fix the prescaler, and suggest with tdoff/tdon/tpdmax/tpdmin (ns) to derive the dead time. Returns PSC, ARR, CCR1, actual frequency and error, duty resolution in bits, DTG and BDTR with the real dead time, high/low-side on times, nearby PSC/ARR alternatives, HAL init code and raw register writes; warnings when a pulse vanishes inside the dead time or the resolution is poor. Use it when setting up half-bridge or motor PWM on an STM32 advanced timer.
sources: ST RM0090 §17.3.10 (PWM mode), §17.3.13 (complementary outputs and dead-time insertion), §17.4.1 (CR1.CKD, CMS), §17.4.18 (TIMx_BDTR.DTG encoding)
ST RM0008 §14.3.10-14.3.11 and §14.4.18 (STM32F1 TIM1/TIM8, same encoding)
Infineon AN2007-04, 'How to calculate and minimize the dead time requirement for IGBTs properly' (dead time = ((td_off,max - td_on,min) + (t_pdd,max - t_pdd,min)) x 1.2)
